newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM threatens to down prince's plane.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM threatens to down prince's plane.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen on Sunday threatened to shoot down any airliner that brought exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh back to Phnom Penh.

"Any plane which dares to carry Sirivudh will be hit. Please tell the world that Hun Sen does not threaten but tells the truth and will dare to do it," Hun Sen said in a speech to flood victims northeast of the capital.
He said tanks and heavy weapons were ready for action in Phnom Penh. "The real battlefield will be Pochentong (airport)."
Sirivudh, the half-brother of King Norodom Sihanouk, was arrested in November 1995 for allegedly plotting to assassinate Hun Sen.
A month later he agreed to go into exile in France rather than go to court but was sentenced in absentia at a trial which international observers branded a travesty.
Sirivudh has said he is determined to return to Cambodia but has not said exactly when. He declined to give a date for his return, saying he was still finalising his plans.
Hun Sen said he would allow Sirivudh to return safely if King Norodom Sihanouk pardoned the prince, but he said that such a decision would promote lawlessness.

Tension is simmering in Cambodia's northwest between military forces loyal to Hun Sen's ex-communist Cambodian People's Party and those supporting its coalition government partner, the FUNCINPEC party, of which Sirivudh is a member.
A FUNCINPEC military commander in Battambang said on Sunday CPP troops had been firing their weapons in the air over the weekend to "show their strength."
No one has been injured, he said, but added: "They can shoot if they like, but if they hit a member of FUNCINPEC or any soldier, I will use force to protect them."
Analysts said Sirivudh's planned return to Cambodia could be a lightning rod in the conflict between Ranariddh and Hun Sen.

Ranariddh said earlier this week that police orders to arrest and jail Sirivudh upon his return came without proper approval, and Hun Sen's war-like rhetoric on Sunday was likely to widen their rift, they said.

Ranariddh, who is serving one week as a monk according to Cambodian royal tradition, was unavailable for comment. He is scheduled to make a one-day pilgrimage to India on Monday as part of his monkhood.
